name: Kernel ASLR Full Randomization Entropy
description: Validates that Address Space Layout Randomization is locked at maximum entropy (Level 2).
attack_vector: Without Level 2 ASLR, the base virtual memory addresses of the user stack, VDSO page, shared memory segments, data segments, and the program heap remain static or partially predictable. Attackers construct deterministic Return-Oriented Programming (ROP) or Return-to-libc payloads that reliably hijack execution flow without needing to guess or brute-force memory offsets.
pass_msg: ASLR is fully enforced (Level 2) - Stack, VDSO, Shared Memory, and Data Segments randomized.
fail_msg: ASLR is weakened or disabled - Memory layout predictable by exploit payloads.

name: Kernel Pointer Leaking (kptr_restrict)
description: Ensures kernel addresses in /proc/kallsyms are completely hidden from unprivileged and sudo users.
attack_vector: Local privilege escalation (LPE) exploits rely on resolving precise kernel symbols (such as commit_creds and prepare_kernel_cred) to elevate an unprivileged shell into root. When kptr_restrict is set to 0 or 1, /proc/kallsyms exposes all kernel text and data symbols directly to attackers, completely bypassing Kernel Address Space Layout Randomization (KASLR).
pass_msg: Kernel pointer restriction enforced (Level 2) - Kernel memory addresses completely obfuscated as zeros.
fail_msg: Kernel pointers exposed to unprivileged users - Aiding local privilege escalation exploit chains.

name: dmesg Information Disclosure (dmesg_restrict)
description: Restricts dmesg kernel ring buffer access exclusively to processes with CAP_SYSLOG or root privileges.
attack_vector: The kernel ring buffer (dmesg) logs hardware events, driver initialization, memory page allocations, and crash stack traces. When unrestricted, unprivileged local users or compromised web services can read dmesg to extract hardware serial numbers, Wi-Fi keys, memory layout leaks from kernel oopses, and debug offsets useful for crafting exploits.
pass_msg: Kernel dmesg buffer restricted to privileged users - Information leakage mitigated.
fail_msg: dmesg buffer readable by regular users - Kernel debug info may leak memory addresses.

name: SYN Flood Denial-of-Service Protection (tcp_syncookies)
description: Enforces TCP SYN cookies to mitigate SYN backlog exhaustion attacks.
attack_vector: In a classical SYN flood attack, an adversary sends a massive volume of spoofed TCP SYN packets without ever completing the 3-way handshake with an ACK. This rapidly exhausts the kernel's half-open connection backlog table, causing the host to reject legitimate inbound connections. TCP SYN cookies encode connection state into the initial sequence number (ISN), completely eliminating the need for half-open backlog memory tables.
pass_msg: TCP SYN cookies active - Host protected against volumetric SYN flood DoS attacks.
fail_msg: TCP SYN cookies disabled - SYN backlog vulnerable to memory exhaustion and denial of service.

name: ICMP Route Redirect Armor
description: Rejects rogue ICMP route redirects that could alter host gateway routing tables.
attack_vector: ICMP redirect packets are traditionally used by routers to notify hosts of more optimal next-hop routes. However, on local shared networks (LAN / Wi-Fi), a malicious node can forge ICMP Type 5 redirect frames to trick the host into routing outbound internet or intranet traffic through the attacker's machine, enabling full Man-In-The-Middle (MITM) packet capture and plaintext credential harvesting.
pass_msg: ICMP redirects ignored - Route table protected against gateway spoofing.
fail_msg: ICMP redirects accepted - Host susceptible to Man-In-The-Middle routing changes.
